So, will it be possible for me to continue with these results and get QTLs?


#QTL analysis with estimated genetic map
> SNP1 <- calc.genoprob(SNP1, step = 2, off.end = 0.0, error.prob = 0.01, map.function = "kosambi", stepwidth = "fixed")

messages.author: 04e62c3b36bb17bf
messages.subject: Re: Understanding scanone results
parts:
Hi Celesta,
There can be a number of reasons for low LOD scores. These include low heritability, only small effect QTL, problems with your genetic map, etc. You could use qtlDesign (https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/qtlDesign/index.html) to figure out how much power your population has to detect QTL. If your population is under-powered you could potentially do multi-trait QTL mapping, which might increase your ability to detect QTL. 

Looking at your QTL peaks, I see lots of peaks at > 400 cM. I haven't seen such long linkage groups in wheat before. But, maybe your DH population has a ton of recombination. It might be worth double checking that your map is estimated correctly and you don't have strange marker orders. 

Hope this helps. 
John
